column1: # Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored; a field containing a comma is double-quoted.
# A rule is **confronted** on a baseline when some observation of its collector carries the fields the
# rule's `match` names and comes within one unsatisfied condition of firing it — the baseline was asked
# the rule's question and answered no. A rule no baseline confronts is quiet there for a reason that

column2: No baseline carries a Security channel. `baseline-elevated-win11` vendors one .evtx file, a LanguagePackSetup operational log, whose records agree with none of this rule's three conditions. Fabricating a Security log to give the gate something to measure is what fixtures/hosts/PROVENANCE.md forbids: a baseline is the claim that a machine like this is unremarkable, and an invented one claims nothing.
column3: A baseline carries a Security channel whose records this project is allowed to publish. fixtures/evtx/PROVENANCE.md forbids capturing from a player machine and says why: a Security record routinely carries a user name, a host name, a source IP, a SID and a command line, records cannot be redacted in place because each is checksummed within its chunk, and both the rendered-record and raw-string scans must be run before anything is vendored. So the capture has to come from a Windows 11 installation made for this purpose — throwaway local account, no network sign-in, nothing personal on it — and not from anyone real. A log like that is expected to hold Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog records on the Security channel that are not 1102, since 1100 is written when the Event Log service stops, which would confront this rule at two conditions of three with no clearing having happened. That expectation is unverified and has to be checked against the captured log.
